task_title: Theme equipment set index, create-new-theme flow, and model-proposed rosters

plan_review.notes: Separate-model plan review (rubber-duck, gpt-5.4) on the set-index + roster-synthesis design. 3 blocking + 1 non-blocking, all adopted: (1) save-plan must derive its target path server-side from the validated plan.id and accept no path field from the client; (2) workflow dispatch must pin --ref, because `gh workflow run` without one silently targets the DEFAULT branch, and init must verify the plan blob exists on that remote ref; (3) authored plans must become immutable once durable state exists for the set id, since the phase state machine is keyed to the roster it was initialized with; (4) non-blocking - the index must distinguish 'no durable state' from 'store unavailable'. Divergence: minor - the storage split and phased flow were unchanged, but the security posture of save-plan and dispatch was materially tightened before implementation.

rounds.notes: Two blocking, one non-blocking, all trust-boundary bypasses. (1) The allowlist was only enforced on /api/select, so a canvas opened with input.setId bound an arbitrary id with no validation. (2) assertPlanOnRef fell through to `cat-file origin/<ref>` when `git fetch` failed, so a stale tracking ref could pass a plan that is no longer on the remote branch. (3) TOCTOU between the store.has() immutability check and the plan write, since init runs on GitHub outside this process's serializer. Fixed: initial setId now goes through selectSet(); fetch fails closed; savePlan snapshots, writes, re-checks, and rolls back on a lost race. 3 regression tests added.

Reviewer verified all three round-1 fixes and found a residual defect in each, plus two new findings. (1) The startup allowlist check ran after listen(), so an abandoned startup leaked a listening server with no close handle - moved before listen(). (2) FETCH_HEAD is shared per repository, so a concurrent git process could make the blob check evaluate the wrong tip - now fetches into a private per-call ref and deletes it in a finally. (3) A throwing store.has() re-check bypassed the rollback entirely, leaving the write on disk - rollback now also runs on a throwing re-check. (4) New blocking: `process.exitCode` alone could leave the CLI hanging on pooled sockets until the bridge's 4-minute spawn timeout - added an unref'd 500ms forced-exit guard, measured at 6.0s for a synth run and 2.5s for a list. (5) New non-blocking: Node's ENOENT messages leaked absolute filesystem paths to the browser - error bodies are now scrubbed of repoRoot and homedir. 2 further regression tests added; reviewer confirmed XSS escaping, command-injection safety, save-plan path derivation, and the bounded repair loop were all clean.
